prompt: Roll up pipe-delimited enrolment rows into a two-level sorted map of department to level to total students, and a sorted map of department to its distinct courses. Complete both methods in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Collectors.groupingBy takes a three-argument form -- classifier, map factory, downstream collector -- and the downstream can be another groupingBy, which is what produces the nested map in one pipeline. Passing TreeMap::new as the factory at both levels is what makes the keys come out sorted. The second method uses the same shape with Collectors.mapping to pull out just the course name, then collectingAndThen with a TreeSet to make the names distinct and sorted before converting the result to a List.
hints: Parse once: map each row to its trimmed fields (row.split("\\|") then trim each piece) so the collectors downstream only deal with clean values.
groupingBy has a three-argument overload: groupingBy(classifier, TreeMap::new, downstream). Put a second groupingBy in the downstream slot to get the nested map, and summingInt at the bottom.
For the course lists, Collectors.mapping extracts the course name, toCollection with a TreeSet makes them distinct and sorted, and collectingAndThen turns that set into a List at the very end.
